target_customer: Teams and individuals building AI agents (v1), later prosumer users of the Sauna AI assistant
problem: Building reliable AI agents required engineers; Wordware let users write natural-language documents as programs, and later pivoted to Sauna, a context-holding assistant that builds software for repeated tasks.
business_model: SaaS subscription (third-party pages conflict on price); Sauna in early access
product_category: AI agent IDE, then AI assistant

founders.name: Filip Kozera
education: University of Cambridge (studied Deep Learning, per YC page)
previous_startups: KRISTALIC (co-founded and exited per YC page)

founders.name: Robert Chandler
prior_employers: Five AI (early engineer, led Offline Perception)
founders.background_notes: Five AI later acquired by Bosch per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Natural-language programming IDE on top of existing LLMs is standard product engineering with hard reliability problems; the company later reported a full architectural rebuild for Sauna.

defensibility.rationale: Agent builders were crowded and built on third-party models; Sauna aims at accumulated user context as a future moat, not yet shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not sourced; Sacra commentary suggests v1 is becoming a feeder to Sauna, which is speculation.

market_need_then: Surge of interest in LLM agents in 2024; evidence is the size of the seed round that investors committed, not customer data.

identity.voice_and_tone: Ambitious and personal; company page says words are the next programming language

branding.brand_signature: Product name Sauna and the 'largest seed in YC history' claim
branding.community_and_virality: Seed round got press (Eureka, Cambridge Engineering) and big-name angels (Paul Graham among them per the company site).

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive-feeling name tied to its original product, wide press on the seed round, but the pivot to Sauna splits the identity.

pivots.why: Company says it announced the pivot internally after a hard six months with a full rebuild; date not stated

outcome_analysis: Wordware raised a 30 million dollar seed in November 2024 led by Spark Capital, called the largest in YC history, riding the 2024 AI agent wave and a strong Cambridge founding team. It then pivoted from the workflow builder to the Sauna assistant, with Sauna in early access per Sacra. No shutdown or later round was verified.
notes: Round confirmed by the company blog and two outlets. Unverified: ZeroGTalent lists 31.9M total with a Series A; simplify.jobs claims 300 corporate customers; Polish press mentions Sauna expansion. Round month inferred from blog dated November 2024; exact day not recorded. Competitor lists found were 2026 aggregators so none recorded as of founding. Sacra pages are AI-generated summaries.
